stories.headline: Rays capitalize on Guardians' errors in Game 4 to even ALCS at 2-2
stories.summary: The Rays evened their ALCS series against the Guardians at two games apiece with a Game 4 win Saturday night.
stories.body:
CLEVELAND -- Jonathan Aranda's single led to two runs in the seventh inning when the ball got by right fielder Chase DeLauter, Nick Martinez pitched 5⅓ innings for his first postseason win, and the Tampa Bay Rays defeated the Cleveland Guardians 7-3 on Saturday night to even the American League Championship Series at 2-2.

Game 5 of the best-of-seven matchup is Sunday in Cleveland before the series shifts back to St. Petersburg, Florida, on Monday. There is no off day for travel after Friday's game was postponed by rain.

Cleveland's Travis Bazzana hit his first postseason home run but also had a fielding error at second on a tough night for the Guardians' defense.

Tampa Bay took a 2-1 lead in the sixth when Junior Caminero lined a double to the left-field wall off Daniel Espino (0-1), then broke open the game in a three-run seventh.

Richie Palacios and Taylor Walls got aboard on base hits and moved into scoring position on a double steal. After Yandy Diaz struck out, Aranda lined a single past a diving Bazzana, who was playing near the grass between first and second, and into right field. Palacios scored, and when DeLauter allowed the ball under his glove, Walls came around from second. Aranda went all the way to third and scored on Chandler Simpson's sacrifice fly.

Aranda had three hits and drove in two runs after going 0-for-10 in the first three games. Diaz had two hits and two RBIs, including a two-run homer in the ninth off Matt Festa, while Simpson and Caminero each drove in a run.

Pitching on a 46-degree night, Martinez (1-0) allowed one run and two hits in his second career postseason start and 10th appearance. After DeLauter's RBI single put Cleveland up 1-0 in the first, Martinez retired 10 straight at one point before walking Bazzana leading off the fifth.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

stories.headline: Jasmine Jasudavicius outpoints Erin Blanchfield in UFC main event
stories.summary: Jasmine Jasudavicius stated her case as a contender in the featherweight division, dominating Erin Blanchfield on the canvas to win by unanimous decision Saturday.
stories.body:
Instability and opportunity permeate the UFC women's flyweight division, which crowned a new champion two weeks ago and has a former two-time champ lurking in the wings while healing from injury. Several other title hopefuls have been jostling to position themselves to go for the gold.

Jasmine Jasudavicius seized the opportunity to make her presence felt among the leading contenders Saturday, dominating Erin Blanchfield on the canvas in a clash of top-10 125-pounders to win by unanimous decision at UFC Fight Night in Edmonton, Alberta.

The fight was the co-main event of a card headlined by Mike Malott's explosive knockout win over Joaquin Buckley. Malott, who like Jasudavicius is from Ontario and had the crowd firmly behind him, landed a knee to the chin that crumbled Buckley, who is No. 8 in the ESPN welterweight rankings and lost his third in a row.

"Hey, guys, I might be soft-spoken," Malott said afterward, "but I'm f---ing hard-hitting."

Malott's knockout came at 2 minutes, 32 seconds of the second round and put a ferocious cap on an event that tied a UFC record with 12 finishes (seven knockouts, five submissions). The other modern-era fight card with a dozen finishes was UFC Fight Night in Belgrade, Serbia, on Aug. 1.

Nevertheless, it was the night's lone bout to go the distance that had the highest stakes. Jasudavicius, No. 8 in the ESPN women's flyweight rankings, pulled off the upset against third-ranked Blanchfield, who came in situated behind only injured former champion Valentina Shevchenko and new titlist Natalia Silva. Blanchfield is also No. 9 in the ESPN women's pound-for-pound top 10.

Jasudavicius (16-4) surely elevated her standing in the 125-pound hierarchy with a robust performance that produced her second straight victory. Both women came in touted as elite grapplers, and Jasudavicius proved to be a step ahead by repeatedly taking the fight to the ground (five takedowns) and threatening submissions from dominant positions for long stretches of the first two rounds.

"I love grappling," she said. "I understand it. I'm pretty good at it. And I like to show what I've got."

Jasudavicius showed enough to impress the judges, getting the nod on all three scorecards (29-28, 29-28, 29-28). The announcement of the verdict drew a roar from the crowd, which was enthusiastically behind the 37-year-old competing in her home country.

"To be able to fight in Canada, you hear the crowd, man. We're about it," Jasudavicius said.

Jasudavicius and Malott were among a dozen Canadian fighters on the card, who went a combined 5-7.

Jasudavicius' victory might not put her in position for an immediate title shot, but she has her sights on a future meeting with the new champ, who defeated her by decision in 2022 in her second UFC fight.

"I want to cross paths with Natalia Silva again," Jasudavicius said. "We had a little bit of history before, so it would be an epic story."

For Blanchfield (14-3), the defeat halted a two-fight winning streak. She outlanded Jasudavicius 62-43 in significant strikes, but the author of five UFC submissions never could get her ground game going. Jasudavicius put Blanchfield on the defensive the whole fight with nearly eight minutes of control time.

stories.headline: Lionel Messi scores twice, takes season tally to 25 in Miami win at Atlanta
stories.summary: Lionel Messi scored two scintillating second-half solo goals to take his MLS-leading tally to 25 as Inter Miami brushed aside hosts Atlanta United 3-1 on Saturday.
stories.body:
Lionel Messi scored two trademark second-half solo goals to take his MLS-leading tally to 25 as Inter Miami brushed aside hosts Atlanta United 3-1 on Saturday.

After Mexico striker Germán Berterame put Miami ahead in the 45th minute, Messi took center stage after the restart with two goals in four minutes.

The first, in the 56th minute, came after Messi drove infield from the right wing and exchanged passes with Berterame on the edge off the penalty area before dancing past a desperate Atlanta defender and firing low into the net.

His second was more of the same. This time, Luis Suárez sent him free on a breakaway and the Argentine forward again bewitched a hapless defender before once more beating Atlanta goalkeeper Lucas Hoyos with his left foot.

Atlanta got a late consolation goal through a penalty from former Miami forward Fafà Picault.

"He never ceases to amaze the world," Miami coach Cristian "Kily" González said of Messi afterward. "I mean, I honestly can't believe that a guy like him, at 39 years old, is doing what he's doing. And what makes me happiest is seeing that he's truly happy. Because he's happy, he gives everything he has. He enjoys himself and feels right at home.

"As I always say, he pushes us to be better every single day. It's an immense joy to have him here. Everyone knows how special our relationship is. Every time I see him, he brings a smile to my face. I'm still constantly amazed by him."

At full time of Saturday's game, Messi had a six-goal lead in the race for MLS' Golden Boot and also had the joint-most assists (15), along with LAFC's Son Heung-Min, having been credited with a secondary assist on Berterame's opener.

Messi is the first player in MLS history to register 15 assists in three consecutive seasons. He now has a goal contribution in 13 straight matches, tying his second-longest streak with club and country in his career.

Saturday's brace also took Messi to 936 career goals, and his coach has no doubts that he can reach the 1,000 milestone.

"Yes, I believe he'll reach 1,000 goals," González said. "I have faith in that. I know he will, because he loves a challenge, he sets challenges for himself and since he's already achieved everything else, this will be no exception."

He added: "He dazzles me with every single action, every time I see him in training. I truly hope he continues to amaze us right up until the day he decides to retire, which, hopefully, won't be for a long time yet."

Messi's performance Saturday gave the eight-time Ballon d'Or winner another fond memory at Atlanta's Mercedes-Benz Stadium. The game marked Messi's first visit there since the 2026 World Cup semifinal in July, when he provided two late assists to propel Argentina to a dramatic win over England.

Messi has four goals in three games since he bid farewell to the Argentina national team in a friendly against Benin earlier this month.

Miami, which clinched a spot in the playoffs Wednesday, has won three straight games and is second in the Eastern Conference behind runaway leader Nashville.

Atlanta, under Gerardo "Tata" Martino, Messi's former coach with Miami and Argentina, is languishing in the 14th spot in the Eastern Conference and facing an uphill battle to make the postseason.

Miami will return to action with a visit to the New York Red Bulls next Saturday.

ESPN's Lizzy Becherano contributed to this report.

stories.headline: Chelsea's Emi Martínez has surgery, will be 'back in a few weeks'
stories.summary: Emi Martínez said he would be "back in a few weeks" after undergoing surgery following a head injury suffered during Chelsea's Premier League win over Everton on Saturday.
stories.body:
Emi Martínez said he would be "back in a few weeks" after undergoing surgery following a head injury suffered during Chelsea's Premier League win over Everton on Saturday.

Martínez, 34, collided with Everton's Jarrad Branthwaite when rushing from his goal to attempt to punch an Everton free kick out of his penalty area in the 67th minute of Chelsea's 2-0 win at the Hill Dickinson Stadium.

Both players received treatment on the pitch, with the Everton defender recovering quickly. Martínez, however, received extended treatment from the Chelsea physios and paramedics before being stretchered from the field while receiving oxygen.

He was replaced by 21-year-old substitute goalkeeper Mike Penders in the 75th minute. Eleven minutes of injury time were added on by the officials at the end of the match following the lengthy stoppage in play.

The Argentina goalkeeper posted a photo of himself in a hospital bed late Saturday night, with the caption: "Thank you all for the messages, the operation went well. The most important thing is that we won and with a bow at 0. We'll be back in a few weeks."

Chelsea coach Xabi Alonso earlier told reporters that Martínez was conscious when leaving the stadium and was taken to hospital for "precautionary tests," adding: "For now, we need to wait."

He added: "It was a concussion, but more than that. I saw just one clip, but we'll have to wait."

Two goals from Pedro Neto ensured Chelsea took all three points from their trip to Merseyside.

"We are really pleased. Shame for Emi, but we wish you all the best. This win is for him," Neto told TNT Sports.

Everton manager David Moyes said: "I just said to TV, I've not seen the Martínez injury yet, so I hope he's fine. I really do. I couldn't even see from the dugout. It just looked as if it was a sharing ball in between a couple of people. I don't know what else happened."

Chelsea's victory put an end to Everton's unbeaten start to the campaign and saw their defense hold firm for the first time this season.

"I'm really pleased with the performance, with the win, with the clean sheet," Alonso said. "There are many positives to build on from today. We knew it was going to be a hard challenge to win in this stadium, but we did many things to deserve the win. I think we got many things right. We were very professional, very solid, and it's good to have this feeling to win this way.

"We needed to feel like we could win in this way -- being solid, being strong, looking in control and going through difficult moments.

"In the first half, there were moments where there were corners and throw-ins and you need to overcome these moments. It's very hard in the Premier League to have full control of the game but you need to make sure you don't lose your shape or your condition, and today we did that really well."

Information from ESPN's Beth Lindop contributed to this story.

stories.headline: Knicks waive Bruce Brown, keep James Wiseman ahead of opener
stories.summary: The Knicks are waiving Bruce Brown and keeping James Wiseman on the roster as the team heads into its regular-season opener, sources told ESPN.
stories.body:
The New York Knicks waived Bruce Brown and will keep James Wiseman on the roster as the team heads into its regular-season opener.

Brown was one of several players on non-guaranteed deals vying for one of New York's final two available roster spots. Tony Bradley, Ochai Agbaji and Drew Eubanks also were waived in recent days.

Wiseman appeared in all four of the Knicks' preseason games and impressed in 24 minutes versus the Toronto Raptors on Tuesday, when he scored 18 points and grabbed 10 rebounds.

According to ESPN's Bobby Marks, the Knicks could have kept Brown and Wiseman, but because they are only $3.2 million below their self-imposed hard cap at the second apron, retaining both players would've been difficult.

Wiseman, 25, will join Karl-Anthony Towns and Andre Drummond in New York's center rotation. The reigning NBA champions lost key reserve big man Mitchell Robinson to the Boston Celtics this past summer via free agency.

The Knicks will begin the NBA's regular season Tuesday when they host the new-look Philadelphia 76ers.

stories.headline: Christian Horner plays down Ferrari links, 'no idea' on Formula 1 return
stories.summary: Christian Horner again played down links to Ferrari as the former Red Bull boss claimed he would be "at peace" if a return to Formula One never happens.
stories.body:
Christian Horner again played down links to Ferrari as the former Red Bull boss claimed he would be "at peace" if a return to Formula One never happens.

Horner, 52, started his speaking tour to help launch his new book, entitled "Drive," at the Barbican in York on Saturday.

He ran through his entire Formula One career, from Red Bull's introduction into the sport through to his controversial exit after the British Grand Prix in 2025.

- Horner: Mercedes' Wolff has it 'easy' at the moment

- Rafael Câmara to Haas: How F1's next rookie could shake up Ferrari's future

- Verstappen finishes 9th in GT World Challenge

But the two-hour show passed without a single mention of the allegations Horner faced during his latter days with the team. The billed Q&A from the audience was delivered in the form of QR-code submitted questions put to Horner by the host.

Red Bull's decision to sack him came a year and a half after he was accused of "inappropriate behaviour" by a female colleague. Horner always denied the accusations and was exonerated for a second time of controlling behaviour by an independent KC. It is a subject covered in the book in a chapter titled "Out come the wolves."

Horner's Red Bull exit ended a 20-year career with the team, where he won eight drivers' and six constructors' titles, and he continues to be linked with a return to the sport.

A recent interview, in which Horner described Ferrari as the biggest brand in F1, reignited links to the Italian giants, but he again moved to talk that down.

"I said 'there's an aura around Ferrari, it's a privilege as a driver, an engineer etc. It is the dream of so many drivers.' I never said it was my bloody dream!" Horner said.

"But the story came out that Ferrari was my dream job. I felt sorry for Fred [Vasseur, Ferrari team principal] because suddenly he was under a lot of pressure."

Horner touched on how he lured design guru Adrian Newey to the team, his relationship with world champion drivers Sebastian Vettel and Max Verstappen and how the organisation of the team changed following the death of Red Bull co-founder Dietrich Mateschitz in 2022.

He described his sacking from Red Bull, days after the Silverstone race, as "brutal."

When the subject of his future came up again, Horner suggested that a return to F1 is not a certainty.

"What excites me most is what is the next chapter going to be and, honestly, I have no idea," Horner added.

"If my time is done in Formula One, I've had a hell of a ride and I did OK. If the right thing comes up to go back, I go back. But I am at peace in myself that if it doesn't I don't have to."

Red Bull are using their own power trains for the first time this season, the culmination of a five-year project launched in 2021 and overseen by Horner until his departure.

Verstappen has won the last two races -- in Malaysia and Singapore -- to deliver the first successes of that project on track and Horner spoke of his pride in seeing the engine come to fruition.

"Seeing that engine come to life and deliver and be reliable ... people thought it would be a joke," he said.

"To see podiums and then the victories in the last two weeks, in its 16th race to win a Grand Prix, I took huge pride in that. Both shareholders contacted me and thanked me."

stories.headline: How Golden State held court to take 1-0 lead over Atlanta in WNBA Finals
stories.summary: Golden State held court 68-64 to take a 1-0 lead over the Atlanta Dream in Game 1 of the WNBA Finals.
stories.body:
SAN FRANCISCO -- Game 1 goes to the Golden State Valkyries.

The No. 2 seed held court 68-64 in Game 1 of the WNBA Finals to take the early lead over the No. 4 seed Atlanta Dream in the best-of-seven series.

Gabby Williams led Golden State with 26 points, including four free throws in the final 1:18 to seal the victory. The back-and-forth game featured seven lead changes.

Allisha Gray paced the Dream with 19 points but didn't score in the fourth quarter when the Dream shot 2-for-20 in the period. Angel Reese had 14 points and 12 rebounds.

The Valkyries, who have won all five playoff games at home this postseason and had the best record at home in the regular season, snapped the Dream's 10-game winning streak, which dated to the regular season.

Both teams seek their first WNBA championship. Game 2 is Monday night back at Chase Center. As the better seed, the Valkyries will host Games 2 and, if necessary, 5 and 7 in a 2-2-1-1-1 format.

ESPN was courtside Saturday with live analysis throughout the game.

Jump to:

Postgame analysis | Relive the action

More:

Finals preview | Top 15 players | Schedule | Offseason guide

(2) Golden State Valkyries 68,

(4) Atlanta Dream 64

How Golden State won the game: Both teams made big runs in this game, which set up a fourth quarter that was all about grit and determination. And also timing. After being outscored 17-9 in the third quarter, the Valkyries outscored the Dream 17-8 in the fourth quarter.

The Dream went just 4-of-25 from 3-point range, with Allisha Gray going 1-of-8. They were 18-of-21 from the foul line, but that was an area where the Valkyries were able to make up ground in the fourth quarter, finishing 11-of-16 from the stripe.

Getting into crunch time, Atlanta seemed to get a little too sped up offensively and took shots too early when it would have helped the Dream to work their offense more. Of course, that's easier said than done against the best defense in the WNBA.

Rebounding ended up being a key factor, as the Valkyries won the board battle 41-35. And Golden State's depth -- much talked about before the series began -- came through. Particularly with Kaila Charles, who played 30 minutes, compiling seven points and 10 rebounds.

Gabby Williams led the way with 26 points, the only Valkyries player in double figures. -- Michael Voepel

What the win means for the Valkyries: They won their first Finals game in their first WNBA Finals appearance. Even when the Dream went on runs, the Valkyries never deviated from their game plan -- and it never felt like they fully lost momentum. Maybe that's also a credit to the noise in Ballhalla.

This game showed an elite level of composure from the Valkyries, and that is a great sign for Golden State. Gabby Williams said that even though the Valkyries trailed with a few minutes left in the game, they had the Dream "right where we wanted them." She said it's because they knew the game would come down to stops.

"That's our bread and butter," Williams added.

If the Valkyries can withstand the Dream's offensive runs and then lock them up on defense, they have a good chance to head to Atlanta with a 2-0 lead. -- Kendra Andrews

What changes do you expect in Game 2? The Dream must win a game on the road if they want to win the title, so winning Game 1 would have given them more of a cushion moving forward. Now, Game 2 feels like a must-win at Chase Center before the series shifts to Atlanta for Games 3 and 4.

Dream coach Karl Smesko sounded confident in his team's ability to turn things around in Game 2. He said Saturday's game didn't come down to what Golden State did, but rather the Dream's loss was the result of one bad defensive stretch and a cold offensive quarter in the fourth.

Still, when the Dream punched first in the opening quarter, they led by only eight points at the end of the period. For Atlanta to even the series Monday, the Dream have to make sure they are executing. They also need more from Angel Reese, who dominated early but was held scoreless in the second half, and Rhyne Howard, who finished with 12 points but shot 3-for-14 from the field and 2-for-9 from 3-point range. -- Andrews

stories.headline: Eagles QB Jalen Hurts on IR due to blood clot, expected to be out indefinitely
stories.summary: The Eagles have placed Jalen Hurts on injured reserve after consultations with numerous doctors and experts, sources told ESPN and NFL Network.
stories.body:
The Philadelphia Eagles have placed Jalen Hurts on injured reserve after consultations with numerous doctors and experts that continued into Saturday, sources told ESPN and NFL Network.

The move will sideline the star quarterback indefinitely, according to sources. The Eagles, who officially announced the move Saturday afternoon, were waiting to make a roster decision until after consulting with medical experts, according to sources.

Ever since Hurts started dealing with the superficial blood clot in his calf, the Eagles have been attempting to explore every option and gather as much information as possible. Hurts has met with doctors and had others review his blood clot and weigh in with their knowledge.

At some time over the past 24 hours, additional information surfaced that made Philadelphia believe the wisest course of action was to place Hurts on IR, giving him the time he needs to heal.

The Eagles have maintained that they wouldn't rush into a decision about Hurts' future, which is why they waited until Thursday to rule out the three-time Pro Bowl quarterback for Sunday's home game against the Carolina Panthers.

Hurts will now miss games against the Panthers, Dallas Cowboys, Washington Commanders and New York Giants before the Eagles have their bye in Week 10, with a chance to fully evaluate their quarterback's health and their team's outlook.

Philadelphia believes the blood clot is treatable, and the ultimate decision about when Hurts returns to play will come from his medical team, with the Eagles ready to follow his lead.

In most cases, blood clots are treated with anticoagulants, otherwise known as blood thinners. A player cannot play while on blood thinners.

In general, the minimum time frame for a moderate dose of anticoagulants is six weeks, sources said. There is a possibility, if the clot is minor enough, that doctors begin with anti-inflammatories only, while continuing to monitor. If the clot were to move, as the team said happened in Hurts' case, blood thinners are often the answer. If the clot were to worsen, blood thinners for roughly three months would be the next course of action.

Some doctors around the NFL who have not examined Hurts believe the blood clot could sideline him for several weeks. One team's doctor texted ESPN: "It is a broad range and nuance based on size and location and hematology evaluation, but could be six weeks." Another team's doctor had a similar estimation.

The Eagles released a lengthy statement Thursday detailing the process that led to the discovery of the blood clot and to Hurts being ruled out for Sunday's game.

While Hurts has been receiving treatment, the Eagles have been working to fortify their roster. Backup quarterback Tanner McKee will start against the Panthers, and rookie Cole Payton was promoted to backup. Philadelphia also signed quarterback Joe Milton off Dallas' practice squad. By NFL rules, Milton must be on the Eagles' roster for three weeks.

This is just the latest sequence in what has been a chaotic stretch for the organization that has included hamstring injuries to running back Saquon Barkley and wide receiver DeVonta Smith, the retirement of future Hall of Fame offensive tackle Lane Johnson and the trade of Pro Bowl center Cam Jurgens.

Amid the injuries and turnover on their offensive line, the Eagles have gotten off to a rough start offensively this season. They enter Sunday in the bottom five in the NFL in points per game (18.4, 29th), total yards per game (262.2, 31st), yards per play (4.5, 30th) and passing yards per game (170.6, 28th).

The Eagles have failed to score 25 points in seven consecutive regular-season games, their longest such streak since Nick Sirianni became their coach before the 2021 season. Philadelphia has gone three-and-out on 38% of its possessions, the highest in the NFL this season.

The Eagles' offense has struggled to stay on the field, specifically in the second half, going three-and-out on 52% of its second-half possessions, which is on pace to be the highest by any NFL team in the past 20 seasons. Philadelphia has been outgained by a league-leading 115 yards per game in the second half this season; the next-worst team in that category is the Indianapolis Colts, who have been outgained by 38 yards per game in the second half.

stories.headline: Lisandro Martínez's Man United comments 'not that far off' but should not have been made - Peter Schmeichel
stories.summary: Former Manchester United goalkeeper Peter Schmeichel has said he believes Lisandro Martínez's criticism of the club's hierarchy is "not that far off."
stories.body:
Former Manchester United goalkeeper Peter Schmeichel has said he believes Lisandro Martínez's criticism of the club's hierarchy is "not that far off" but added he would not have liked hearing a teammate sound off in public.

Schmeichel was criticised for his handling of a post-match interview with Martínez in the aftermath of Tuesday night's 2-0 Champions League loss to Atlético Madrid, when the Argentina defender turned his fire on the club's hierarchy and named director of football Jason Wilcox as one of those from whom he "expects more."

Martínez spoke first to Amazon Prime's Gabriel Clarke before Schmeichel interviewed him for U.S. broadcaster CBS, with the defender repeating many of his criticisms while Schmeichel appeared to be trying to move Martínez on from the topic.

On Thursday Martínez issued a public apology for his comments and United said the matter was considered closed after the 28-year-old met with manager Michael Carrick, Wilcox and the club's hierarchy.

But inevitably the issue dominated Carrick's news conference on Friday with the substance of Martínez's comments still being debated.

Speaking on The Overlap Daily, Schmeichel said: "I would not like any teammate ever to go out and talk like that. Unless it was Bryan Robson... No, I wouldn't. I absolutely wouldn't like that.

"In the dressing rooms I was in, you were accountable. It just didn't happen very often that somebody stepped out of line, and of course we had a manager [Sir Alex Ferguson] who would not allow you to step out of line. He would react to that straight away...

"It's not that I completely disagree with what [Martínez] says. That's the other thing."

- Man United 'a circus' amid Lisandro Martínez rant - Roy Keane

Schmeichel then added: "Without going into too much detail about what Martínez said, some of the things he said are not far off.

"Look at the promising teams: Manchester City a long time ago, Arsenal for the past six years, Liverpool under Jürgen Klopp -- what did they do that suddenly changed the dynamics and changed their fortunes? They started at the back.

"They got in a goalkeeper, back four, a centre midfield player. They built that foundation, made it solid, and then they started to bring the creative players in. They've all done it... Built from the back. We've done the opposite, built from the front."

stories.headline: NRL transfer whispers: Rivals keeping tabs on Dragons' Tu
stories.summary: The NRL season may be over, but the player market is already heating up ahead of November 1. Isaac Issa has news from the Dragons on some key outside backs
stories.body:
The NRL season may be over, but the player market is already heating up ahead of November 1, with clubs beginning to shape their rosters for 2027 and beyond.

From player movement to changes behind the scenes, ESPN NRL Insider Isaac Issa has the latest whispers from around the competition.

Rivals keeping tabs on Dragons' Tu

Multiple clubs are monitoring St George Illawarra outside back Setu Tu, with the Dragons yet to begin talks over a contract extension.

Tu is contracted until the end of 2027 and is expected to test the open market from November 1, when rival clubs can negotiate a deal for 2028 and beyond.

The former Warriors outside back joined the Dragons on a development contract this season and is set to move into the club's top 30 squad in 2027.

His ability to cover multiple positions across the backline adds to his appeal as clubs assess their recruitment options.

Rivals monitor Patea as open market looms
Penrith young gun Luron Patea is expected to test the open market from November 1, with multiple clubs keeping tabs on the promising prop.

Patea is contracted until the end of 2027, but the Panthers are yet to begin talks over an extension, leaving rival clubs poised to explore a deal for 2028 and beyond.

Penrith have not granted Patea permission to negotiate with other clubs before November 1.

The Panthers junior made his NRL debut in 2024 and has shown promise during his first-grade opportunities, providing another emerging option in Penrith's forward pack.

He is among several Panthers players approaching the final year of their contracts, with veteran prop Moses Leota also unsigned beyond 2027.

Roosters eye Dockar-Clay reunion
The Roosters have shown interest in a potential return for Zach Dockar-Clay as they explore options to bolster their hooking and utility depth.

ESPN understands the 31-year-old has emerged as an option following his departure from Manly, with discussions remaining at an early stage.

Dockar-Clay spent the 2024 and 2025 seasons with the Roosters before joining the Sea Eagles on a one-year deal for 2026.

Manly confirmed his departure last month after a season in which he claimed the club's NSW Cup best-and-fairest award.

Bostock brushes Dragons links

Dolphins star Jack Bostock has dismissed recent links between himself and the Dragons, admitting this isn't the first time he'd been floated for a club switch.

"I've been linked to a few a clubs," Bostock admitted.

"I don't know about [the Dragons links]."

He said that while he "obviously sees it in the media," his sole focus is the Kangaroos.

Sloan's Dragons stay still a possibility

Tyrell Sloan could yet remain at St George Illawarra next season, with discussions ongoing over a potential stay despite his planned move to Castleford.

There is interest in keeping Sloan at the Dragons, but several hurdles remain before that can become a reality.

Roster space and salary cap room would need to be worked through, while any arrangement would also require Castleford to agree to release him.

Sloan previously admitted he would "love to" remain in the NRL when speaking to Channel Nine in August, after his Castleford deal had been announced.

No agreement has been reached and a stay is far from guaranteed.

stories.headline: Rays capitalize on Guardians errors, win 7-3 to tie ALCS at 2-2
stories.summary: — Jonathan Aranda's single led to two runs in the seventh inning when the ball got by right fielder Chase DeLauter, Nick Martinez pitched 5 1/3 innings for his first postseason win and the Tampa Bay Rays defeated the Cleveland Guardians 7-3 Saturday...
stories.body:
CLEVELAND -- — Jonathan Aranda's single led to two runs in the seventh inning when the ball got by right fielder Chase DeLauter, Nick Martinez pitched 5 1/3 innings for his first postseason win and the Tampa Bay Rays defeated the Cleveland Guardians 7-3 Saturday night to even the AL Championship Series at 2-2.


Game 5 of the best-of-seven matchup is Sunday in Cleveland before the series shifts back to St. Petersburg, Florida, on Monday. There is no off day for travel after Friday's game was postponed by rain.


“It means a lot because we know that we play well at home in front of our fans. We’ve got a huge game, another swing game tomorrow,” Rays manager Kevin Cash said.


Cleveland's Travis Bazzana hit his first postseason home run but also had a fielding error at second on a tough night for the Guardians' defense.


The first four hitters in the Rays order — Yandy Díaz, Aranda, Chandler Simpson and Junior Caminero — had six of the Rays' 11 hits and drove in six runs after they went 7 for 41 with three RBI the first three ALCS games.


Aranda had three hits and drove in two runs after going 0 for 10 in the first three games. Diaz had two hits and two RBI, including a two-run homer in the ninth off Matt Festa, while Simpson and Caminero each drove in a run.


“A lot of really good at-bats. A lot of hard hits,” Cash said. “But overall, just happy that Junior squared some balls up, Aranda came through in a big way for us and then Yandy there at the end with a two-run, add-on homer.”


Pitching on a 46-degree night, Martinez (1-0) allowed one run and two hits in his second career postseason start and 10th appearance. After DeLauter's RBI single put Cleveland up 1-0 in the first, Martinez retired 10 straight at one point before walking Bazzana leading off the fifth.


Tampa Bay took a 2-1 lead in the sixth when Caminero lined a double to the left-field wall off Daniel Espino (0-1), then broke open the game in a three-run seventh.


Richie Palacios and Taylor Walls got aboard on base hits and moved into scoring position on a double steal. After Díaz struck out, Aranda lined a single past a diving Bazzana, who was playing near the grass between first and second, and into right field. Palacios scored and when DeLauter allowed the ball under his glove, Walls came around from second. Aranda went all the way to third and scored on Simpson's sacrifice fly.


“It looked like it may have snaked on him or just skipped by him, took his eye off of it," Cleveland manager Stephen Vogt said. "A couple unfortunate plays for us tonight that we usually complete and just weren’t able to do it.”


Bazzana homered in the seventh against Ian Seymour and Brayan Rocchio added an RBI single as Cleveland closed to 5-3.


Shawn Armstrong opened and struck out one batter in the first inning before giving way to Foster Griffin.


Up next
Cleveland rookie Parker Messick (0-2, 3.09 ERA) will make his fourth start this postseason. He went five innings and was charged with three unearned runs in Tuesday's 3-1 loss in Game 2. Tampa Bay's Drew Rasmussen (1-0, 1.29 ERA) allowed two runs over six innings in Game 1 and struck out seven before the Guardians rallied for a 7-3 victory.

stories.headline: Griezmann has 2 goals, 1 assist for Orlando City in 4-1 win over DC United
stories.summary: Antoine Griezmann had two goals and an assist, Martín Ojeda added a goal and an assist, and Orlando City beat D.C. United 3-1 on Saturday night.
stories.body:
ORLANDO, Fla. -- - Antoine Griezmann had two goals and an assist, Martín Ojeda added a goal and an assist, and Orlando City beat D.C. United 3-1 on Saturday night.

Griezmann has 12 goals and seven assists in 14 MLS appearances and is the first player in league history with a goal contribution in 12 of his first 14 career games.

Marco Pasalić scored a stoppage-time goal for Orlando (12-13-5). Maxime Crépeau had three saves.

Tai Baribo converted from the penalty spot in first-half stoppage time for D.C. (7-10-12).

Ojeda, just inside the top of the 18-yard box, chipped a first-touch pass over four defenders to a charging Griezmann on the give-and-go for a first-touch finish from 7 yards out to make it 1-0 in the 15th minute.

Ojeda flicked a back-heel volley, off a feed from Griezmann, past goalkeeper Sean Johnson and inside the left post to give Orlando a two-goal lead in the 22nd.

Griezmann intercepted a misplayed pass by Kye Rowles in D.C.'s defensive third, took two dribbles and rolled a shot into the net to make it 3-1 in the 50th minute.

Johnson finished with three saves.

Up next D.C.: Plays Wednesday at Cincinnati.

Orlando: Hosts New York City next Saturday.

stories.headline: Mikel Arteta: 'Big believer' Arsenal's Kai Havertz can score 30 goals a season
stories.summary: Mikel Arteta has said he is a "big believer" that Kai Havertz can be Arsenal's 30-goal-a-season man.
stories.body:
Mikel Arteta has said he is a "big believer" that Kai Havertz can be Arsenal's 30-goal-a-season man.

Havertz is set to lead the line for Arsenal in their clash at Nottingham Forest on Sunday as he continues to be preferred to the out-of-favour Viktor Gyökeres.

The German joined Arsenal from Chelsea in 2023, scoring 14 goals in his first season at the Emirates Stadium before netting 15 in the following campaign.

A hamstring injury saw him miss the concluding four months of that season before both hamstring and knee problems restricted him to just 24 appearances across all competitions last term, with a return of seven goals.

The 27-year-old has started all of Arsenal's league games so far, scoring twice in the Premier League champions' opening three games, but has not found the back of the net since -- a barren streak of five matches.

However, speaking ahead of Sunday's contest at the City Ground, Arteta insisted Havertz can hit as many as 30 goals a season.

"He has that ability," Arteta said. "That is why he is playing there as well, and that is why we signed him.

"He needs that volume of games and actions, and if you give him that, I am a big believer that yes, he can do it.

"His football IQ is something else. He understands everything at such speed, and he can break down information better probably than anyone else on the team.

- Mikel Arteta defends Viktor Gyökeres after goalless start to season

- Mikel Merino: I am 'fortunate to be alive' after Dortmund bus attack

- Eberechi Eze to perform Cristiano Ronaldo-inspired celebration after loss to IShowSpeed

"That's something that's not easy to say especially when we talk about a striker. He was out for a long period of time last season and to get back at the highest level is not easy and it can take time.

"But Kai has done it almost immediately from pre-season and I'm not surprised because his mentality is top. I value him a lot."

Gyökeres was handed just his third start of the season in Arsenal's Champions League match against Lille on Tuesday night.

The Sweden international was withdrawn midway through the second half having made little impact on the game.

Gyökeres scored 97 times across 102 appearances for former club Sporting Lisbon, but he is yet to find the back of net in his seven games this season.

"That's a very personal question," Arteta said, when asked if Gyökeres, who struck 21 times in his debut campaign for the Gunners, is low on confidence.

"What he transmits to me is an incredible will and determination and work-rate to improve and help the team.

"That's Viktor every single day, regardless of his position, whether he scores a goal or not, and that's why he's always an option to play.

"We are trying to help him as much as possible. He has some very good moments, but it's very small margins, and scoring, or not scoring, changes the narrative."

stories.headline: 76ers, needing frontcourt help, convert 7-foot-6 Tacko Fall to two-way contract
stories.summary: The 76ers, dealing with injuries in the frontcourt, have converted center Tacko Fall to a two-way contract.
stories.body:
PHILADELPHIA -- The 76ers have converted center Tacko Fall to a two-way contract, the team announced Saturday.

Last month, the Sixers signed the 7-foot-6 center to an Exhibit 10 deal, and injuries to the frontcourt likely led to Fall getting this spot.

Ariel Hukporti, projected to be the Sixers' backup center, suffered a season-ending right Achilles tear in the preseason. Center Adem Bona, potentially the next man up, has been sidelined with a foot injury, and Dominick Barlow has battled back soreness that kept him out of the preseason.

Fall hasn't played in the NBA since the 2021-22 season, when he was with the Cleveland Cavaliers. This will be his fourth season in the NBA. He played his first two in Boston with new Sixers forward Jaylen Brown.

Fall, 30, most recently played for the Ningbo Rockets of the Chinese Basketball Association.

stories.headline: Max Verstappen clinches top-10 finish at first GT World Challenge
stories.summary: Max Verstappen fought back from 24th to ninth at the GT World Challenge after his hopes of a podium finish were derailed by a drive-through penalty.
stories.body:
Max Verstappen fought back from 24th to ninth at the GT World Challenge after his hopes of a podium finish were derailed by a drive-through penalty.

A week after claiming his second consecutive Formula One victory in as many races at the Singapore Grand Prix, the four-time world champion was back in the cockpit, this time for a three-hour endurance event in Portugal.

- 'Chucky' Verstappen is back. Luckily for Antonelli and Mercedes, it's too late

Verstappen's teammate, British driver Ben Barnicoat, delivered an encouraging opening stint to move up five places from 13th on the grid.

He handed over to compatriot Chris Lulham who progressed to sixth at the Portimao circuit in the Algarve, which will return to the F1 calendar next season.

However, Lulham was hit with a drive-through penalty when he sent Luca Stolz spinning as they duelled for fifth place.

Lulham served his sanction before Verstappen assumed driving duties, but the Dutchman's team were now out of contention and in 24th -- with only 45 minutes left.

However, Verstappen charged to 15th with a quarter of an hour remaining, and he then managed to make up another six places before the chequered flag following an impressive cameo.

Verstappen will be bidding to make it a hat-trick of F1 victories when he returns to his Red Bull at next weekend's United States Grand Prix in Austin.
